citation: Photograph of Martha L. (Mattie) Williamson, head and shoulders, captioned 'Mattie Williamson in the 1890s', reproduced in Glessner House Museum, 'Mattie Williamson, the Glessners' beloved cook', The Story of a House (blog), 31 March 2020.
author: photographer not named in the post
repository: Glessner House Museum (the post does not say who owns the original print; it says the museum has 'rich archival resources about the live-in staff' and that Mattie's restored room now shows 'several Williamson family photos'). The copy used here is the post's full-size image, 1050 x 1050 px.
locator: The first image in the post, captioned 'Mattie Williamson in the 1890s'. Her face, close to frontal and turned very slightly to her left, fills x 370-665, y 215-560 of the 1050 x 1050 copy (about 280 px across, cheek to cheek).
rights_note: The post gives no credit line or rights statement for this image. The photograph was made in the 1890s by its caption; a photograph made before 1906 is out of copyright in the United States whether or not it was published (published before 1931, or unpublished and more than 120 years old with no named author). The museum's digitisation adds no new copyright under US law for a faithful copy. Credit as: Glessner House Museum. The museum may hold the original and could be asked for a better scan.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-07. The post fetched directly from glessnerhouse.blogspot.com (HTTP 200, no bot check); the image fetched from blogger.googleusercontent.com at its '/s0/' (original-size) address, which returned 1050 x 1050 px; the post itself links the '/s1600/' size. The post's text gives her birth as 23 October 1859 in Inverness, Centre-du-Quebec, Canada, to John and Mary (Duff) Williamson, both Irish-born emigrants to Canada, and says she 'was 53 at the time of her marriage' (26 December 1912). The household record does not yet carry her age or birthplace.
note: A sepia head-and-shoulders portrait of a woman in her thirties: dark wavy hair centre-parted and drawn up, dark eyes looking at the camera, a straight nose, a full lower face and rounded chin; a dark high-necked bodice with very large light-coloured puffed and ruffled shoulder sleeves (the leg-o'-mutton fashion of about 1893-1897) and a ruffled trim down the front. The background is vignetted. The image as posted is evenly sepia-toned and looks retouched or sharpened in places (hair edge, eyes); treat fine texture with care. By her birth date she was in her thirties in the 1890s and 44 in 1904. Also in the same post: a group photograph by George Glessner, 'Mattie is seated at far left in this photo of the servants heading out for their annual picnic to the Flume, located near The Rocks, probably 1893' (900 x 598 px as posted; her face there is about 15 px, too small to use).
what_it_supplies: the proportions of Mattie Williamson's face (eyes, nose, mouth, chin, right ear) as one photograph shows them
how she wore her hair in the 1890s, centre-parted and drawn up
what_it_does_not_supply: her face at 44, the scene year (the photograph is from the 1890s, ten or so years earlier)
her colouring (sepia; the toning may be the museum's)
her working dress: this is a studio portrait in her best clothes, not a cook's apron and cap
